meta.thesis: All Y'Alls does not need more doors - it needs shoppers who try it once to come back, and The Smarter Switch turns H-E-B shelf space into repeat buyers.
meta.variant_angle: Smarter Switch rev1 (DFW H-E-B test + Amazon review rescue)

business_problem: All Y'Alls is in 450+ stores and 6 years into H-E-B, but shoppers who find it on Amazon rate it 3.0-4.2 while the brand's own site reviews average 4.95 - and most Amazon listings show 'currently unavailable.' Trial is not converting into conviction, and availability is not supporting the reviews it does get.

objectives.text: Drive 1,500 attributed purchases (H-E-B coupon + online code) in 45 days, and lift units per store 25% at 6 demo stores vs. 6 control stores
Hand out 2,400 in-store samples and generate 6,000 coupon claims
Reach 1.0M DFW/Texas impressions and lift aided awareness by 10 points among surveyed shoppers

findings.finding: Content analysis of 139 public site reviews (collected 2026-11-07): 73% mention taste/flavor unprompted, average rating 4.95/5, complaints only 6%
findings.therefore: Demo Days and creator taste-offs lead the campaign - product experience, not awareness, is the conversion lever

findings.finding: 37% of 139 reviews mention vegan/vegetarian/diet context, yet the top verbatim praise is 'texture is spot on' from a 12-year plant-based eater - and 5% explicitly compare it to meat jerky
findings.therefore: Position it as a jerky upgrade for everyone, not a vegan product - the meat-jerky shopper is the growth market

findings.finding: Only 2% of 139 reviews mention discovering All Y'Alls in a store; most buyers find it online or by subscription
findings.therefore: Retail trial must be manufactured at the shelf (demos, clip strips, coupons) because organic retail discovery is weak

findings.finding: 19% of 139 reviews mention repeat purchase, bulk, or buying again; price complaints are only 1%
findings.therefore: Campaign ends with a repeat-purchase/bundle offer, not just trial - and no discount-led positioning is needed

findings.finding: Audit (8 public sources, 2026-11-07): 6+ years in H-E-B, sales +104% across 138 H-E-B stores in 2020-21, 450+ retail doors, but Amazon store page shows most listings 'currently unavailable' rated 3.0-4.2
findings.therefore: The problem is trial-to-conviction off the brand's own site - fix availability and review proof at Amazon, not just awareness

findings.finding: Amazon ratings 3.0-4.2 across ~10 listings (~2,400 reviews) vs. site 4.95 (n=139): a full-point gap between channels
findings.therefore: In-store demos and creator taste-offs generate the 'texture is spot on' proof that repairs the Amazon rating gap

programs.name: Smarter Switch Demo Days
programs.mechanic: 12 weekend demo shifts at 6 DFW H-E-B test stores; sample cups beside the meat-snack/jerky set; QR to the '$2 off 2 bags' coupon. 6 matched control stores get the coupon but no demos or clip strip, isolating the in-store effect.

programs.name: The Aisle Upgrade
programs.mechanic: Pitched to H-E-B's snack buyer in October-November: clip strip inside the meat-snack set at 6 test stores, shelf talker, and '$2 off 2 bags' app coupon at DFW H-E-B stores carrying All Y'Alls. Fallback if declined: demos + brand's own printable coupon.

programs.name: Would You Know It's Not Meat?
programs.mechanic: 3 DFW food creators run blind taste-offs: All Y'Alls vs. the jerky they actually buy. Reveal at the end. Link goes to a store finder + coupon, or the online 3-pack with code SMARTERSWITCH. #ad disclosure on every post.

programs.name: Made in Texas, Backed by Science
programs.mechanic: Brett Christoffel's Cross Roads-to-450-stores story plus the surgeon-investor credential (Dr. Rizwan Bukhari) in 3 short videos and 3 emails/SMS to the existing list, each ending with the store finder and the 3-pack code. Includes an Amazon review-rescue insert card driving recent buyers to the site experience.

assumptions.text: Blended net revenue per purchase $20: 50% retail coupon purchases at ~$6 net (2 bags x ~$4 wholesale minus $2 coupon) + 50% online 3-packs at $24-26 (site $24, Amazon ~$19-26) with code discount; confirm wholesale price with company
Blended gross margin 55%: plant-protein COGS lower than meat jerky; DTC 3-pack at $24 carries ~$13+ GP; confirm with company financials
H-E-B store-level baseline velocity unknown; measured week 0 via shelf audit + company sell-through data
Impressions 1.0M = ~670K paid at ~$6 CPM ($4,000) + ~330K creator views (3 creators); 1.5% click rate; 10% click-to-purchase (validate week 1). In-store exposure not counted in the funnel
All Y'Alls and H-E-B would approve in-store demos and a digital coupon (proposed, not confirmed)
DFW food micro-creators (10K-80K followers): ~$750 per video incl. product
In-store demo shift ~$200 (4-hr demo staff via sampling agency + product for ~200 samples)
$2 off 2 bags manufacturer coupon; its cost is netted out of revenue per purchase (A1), not a separate line
Production (shelf talkers, clip strips, sample cups, design) ~$700 via local print shop quotes
Email/SMS + landing page + Amazon insert cards ~$300 for the campaign window
Repeat: 30% of campaign buyers buy once more within 90 days at the same blended gross profit (~$11); confirm with company data
600K bags sold since 2018 across 450+ doors implies low single-digit bags/store/week; exact figure needs company sell-through data
Demo-day purchases (~20% of 2,400 sampled shoppers = ~480) are upside not counted in the funnel
DFW H-E-B stores carrying All Y'Alls exist (6-year H-E-B relationship, brand is Cross Roads TX); exact door count confirmed in week-0 shelf audit
Online offer: 3-pack at $24 with 20% off code SMARTERSWITCH; site offers free shipping over $30

slides.title: Campaign Overview
bullets: Thesis: All Y'Alls does not need more doors - it needs shoppers who try it once to come back [O1].
Problem: 450+ stores and 6 years in H-E-B, yet Amazon shoppers rate it 3.0-4.2 vs. 4.95 on the brand's own site [S1][S5][R5][R6].
Opportunity: 73% of site reviewers praise taste unprompted - the product converts; the problem is reaching meat-snack shoppers [R1].
Solution: 'The Smarter Switch' puts All Y'Alls in the jerky shopper's decision at DFW H-E-Bs and online [O1].
45-day goal: 1,500 attributed purchases and +25% units per store vs. control - the test still runs if the clip strip is declined [O1].
slides.notes: Open with the paradox: the brand is everywhere but Amazon shoppers rate it a full point lower. The problem is not distribution - it is what happens after trial.

slides.title: The Product
bullets: Plant-protein jerky ('The Smarter Jerky') made from whole non-GMO soybeans; 15-17g protein + 8-9g fiber per 2.69 oz bag, 0mg cholesterol [S1].
Four bold Texas flavors: Jalapeño BBQ, Black Pepper & Sea Salt, Prickly Pear Teriyaki, Prickly Pear Chipotle - each named for a Texas region [S1].
Shelf price ~$8/bag, 3-packs $24 online; sold DTC, on Amazon, and in 450+ retail doors incl. H-E-B, Kroger, 7-Eleven, Whole Foods [S1][S2][S4].
Backed by Dr. Rizwan Bukhari, a Texas vascular surgeon and PCRM member, who is Medical Director AND investor; portion of every sale supports Rowdy Girl Sanctuary [S5].

visual.desc: Flat-lay of the four flavor bags with a torn-open bag showing jerky texture

slides.notes: Stress the texture reviews keep praising - 'texture is spot on' - because that is what wins over meat jerky buyers.

slides.title: The Company & Its Position
bullets: Founded by Brett Christoffel in Cross Roads, TX (2018); ~6 employees; 600,000+ bags sold; bootstrapped [S1][S2][S3].
6+ years in H-E-B; won 1st place plant-based / 6th of 830 in H-E-B Quest for Texas Best 2019; sales +104% across 138 H-E-B stores in 2020-21 [S2].
Competitors: Jack Link's, Chomps, Perchik's own plant-jerky set - All Y'Alls is the only Texas-born national plant jerky [S8].
Position: jerky upgrade for everyone - plant protein with the chew and bold flavor of jerky, not a 'vegan alternative' [S1][R2].

visual.desc: Left: distribution growth (2018 launch -> 450+ doors, 600K bags) vs. channel rating gap (site 4.95 vs Amazon 3.0-4.2). Right: positioning map (x = meat jerky to plant protein, y = niche vegan to mainstream snack) with Jack Link's, Chomps, and All Y'Alls alone in 'plant protein, mainstream snack'

slides.notes: This is our credibility slide: distribution is proven, but the channel-rating gap is the problem we are solving.

slides.title: Campaign Objectives
bullets: O1 (primary): 1,500 attributed purchases (750 H-E-B coupon + 750 online) and +25% units per store at 6 demo stores vs. 6 control [O1].
Baseline: week-0 shelf count via audit + company sell-through data [A3].
O2 (consideration): 2,400 in-store samples and 6,000 coupon claims [O2].
O3 (awareness): 1.0M Texas impressions and +10 points aided awareness [O3].

visual.desc: O1-O3 with funnel stage, metric, target, and test-vs-control design

slides.notes: One primary objective - bags sold - measured against control stores, so the client sees lift, not noise.

slides.title: Target Market
bullets: P1 Flexitarian Jerky Fans, 18-34: DFW/Texas jerky buyers open to plant protein; skeptical of 'vegan' labels; buy on taste and macros [S8][R2].
P2 Health-Conscious H-E-B Parents, 30-50: weekly H-E-B shoppers wanting no-cholesterol, high-fiber snacks kids will actually eat [S5][S9].
Both share one need: jerky that tastes like jerky but is smarter - the reason reviewers say 'texture is spot on' [R1][R2].
Market: 6 in 10 US households buy plant-based foods; meat snacks +11.3% to $6.4B while plant-based meat fell 10% [S6][S7][S8].

visual.desc: Two persona cards (P1, P2) with photo, demographics, psychographics, and media habits

slides.notes: Interactive moment: show the two persona cards printed side by side.

slides.title: Research Method & Results
bullets: Secondary (complete): company site, StartupCPG interview, LinkedIn, Faire wholesale, Amazon store page - 10 sources [S1][S2][S3][S4][S5].

Primary, no-survey (complete): keyword-coded analysis of 139 public site reviews [R1][R4] and a public distribution/digital-shelf audit of 8 sources [R5][R6] [S12]; survey/interviews not run - reviews skew positive (self-selected buyers).

Key results: taste dominates reviews, complaints only 6% [R1]; 37% cite diet/vegan context but the praise is texture [R2]; only 2% found it in a store [R3]; H-E-B relationship strong but Amazon ratings lag a full point [R5][R6].
Influences: protein-snack boom (social), flexitarian movement (cultural), food inflation (economic), retail app coupons (technological) [S6][S7][S9].
slides.notes: Name the methods and sample sizes out loud. The Amazon-vs-site rating gap is the finding judges will remember.

slides.title: Insights -> Campaign Decisions
bullets: Finding: 73% of 139 reviews volunteer taste unprompted; complaints are only 6% [R1] -> demos and taste-offs lead, not awareness ads.
Finding: only 2% discovered it in a store; most buyers find it online [R3] -> retail trial must be manufactured at the shelf.
Finding: Amazon 3.0-4.2 vs. site 4.95 - a full-point channel gap [R5][R6] -> generate 'texture is spot on' proof where shoppers look.
Finding: 37% cite vegan/diet context but 5% compare it to meat jerky [R2] -> sell it as a jerky upgrade, not a vegan product.
Finding: 19% reorder and price complaints are 1% [R4] -> end with a bundle/repeat offer, not a discount.
slides.notes: Every decision traces to evidence. Point at the arrows, not the text.

slides.title: Campaign Strategy
bullets: Big idea: The Smarter Switch - jerky lovers don't have to give up jerky to eat smarter. Message: 'Love jerky? Switch to the Smarter Jerky.'
Positioning: for jerky shoppers who want the same chew and bold flavor with plant protein, fiber, and no cholesterol, All Y'Alls is the upgrade [S1][R2].
IMC mix: Paid (geo social) + Earned (Texas founder story + surgeon-investor) + Shared (#SmarterSwitch taste-off duets) + Owned (email/SMS, shelf talkers).
Push-pull: H-E-B gets a measurable velocity test (push); shoppers get samples and a coupon (pull) [O1][O2].

visual.desc: Key visual: split frame - beef jerky aisle on left, All Y'Alls bag glowing on right, 'The Smarter Switch' lockup

slides.notes: Point to the positioning statement. 'Not a vegan product - a jerky upgrade' is the line a competitor can't copy because their brand is built on the niche.

slides.title: Program 1: Smarter Switch Demo Days
bullets: The Smarter Switch in person: 12 weekend demo shifts at 6 DFW H-E-B test stores; 6 control stores get the coupon only [O1][O2].
Mechanic: sample cups at the jerky/meat-snack set; QR code to '$2 off 2 bags'; 200 samples per shift = 2,400 total [A7][A8].
Why: 73% of reviewers say taste is why they buy - and only 2% found it in a store, so the shelf is where discovery must happen [R1][R3].
Measured: QR scans per store and units per store vs. control stores [O1].

visual.desc: Demo table mockup: green tablecloth, 'The Smarter Switch' banner, sample cups, QR sign

slides.notes: Interactive moment: hand the judge the printed shelf talker and sample-cup sleeve.

slides.title: Program 2: The Aisle Upgrade
bullets: The Smarter Switch on the shelf: proposed clip strip inside the H-E-B meat-snack set at 6 test stores [O1].
Sell-in: pitched to H-E-B's snack buyer Oct-Nov as a 6-week velocity test; if the clip strip is declined, demos + brand's printable coupon still run the test - the leg shrinks, not collapses [O1].
App coupon at DFW H-E-B stores carrying All Y'Alls: 'Love jerky? Switch to the Smarter Jerky. $2 off 2 bags.' [A8][A16][O2]
Why: meat snacks are growing 11.3% - put the plant jerky where those shoppers already are [S7][S8].
slides.notes: This is a proposal to H-E-B's buyer, framed as a 6-week velocity test with control stores; the fallback keeps the campaign alive if they say no.

slides.title: Program 3: Taste-Off + Made in Texas
bullets: The Smarter Switch online: 3 DFW food creators run blind All Y'Alls vs. beef jerky taste-offs; fans duet with #SmarterSwitch [O1][O3].
Every video links to the store finder + coupon or the online 3-pack (code SMARTERSWITCH) with #ad disclosure [A17].
Made in Texas, Backed by Science: Brett Christoffel's Cross Roads-to-450-stores story plus Dr. Bukhari's surgeon-investor credential in 3 videos and 3 emails/SMS [S2][S3][S5].
Amazon review-rescue: insert card in recent Amazon orders driving buyers to the site experience - repairing the 3.0-4.2 vs 4.95 gap [R5][R6].

slides.title: Proposed Budget & Financial Viability
bullets: Total $10,000: paid social $4,000 [A4]; creators 3 x $750 = $2,250 [A6]; demos 12 x $200 = $2,400 [A7]; production $700 [A9]; tools $300 [A10]; contingency $350 [A11].
Funnel: 1.0M impressions x 1.5% x 10% = 1,500 purchases; half H-E-B coupon (~$6 net), half online 3-packs (~$20 net) = $20 avg, $30K [A1][A4].
The $2 coupon is manufacturer-funded, already netted in blended revenue - no separate line [A1][A8].
Gross profit at 55% = $16.5K; profit ROI 65%; ROAS 5.0x on $6.25K ad spend [A2].
Conservative (50%): 750 purchases, ROI ~-18%; 30% repeat in 90 days reaches ~break-even [A13]. Upside: ~480 demo-day purchases [A15].
slides.notes: Lead with honesty: in-window it breaks even; the return comes from repeat buyers and from fixing the Amazon rating gap. Then show the test-vs-control design that proves it.

slides.title: Impact & Measurement
bullets: O1: attributed purchases; baseline 0; target 1,500; H-E-B coupon + Shopify code reports; weekly [O1].
O1: units per store per week, demo vs. control; baseline week-0 audit [A3]; target +25%; retailer data; weekly [O1].
O2: samples and claims; baseline 0; target 2,400 and 6,000; tally sheets + coupon platform; weekly [O2].
O3: 1.0M impressions; aided awareness baseline measured at week 0, post-campaign survey of 150 shoppers; target +10 pts [O3].
Trigger: under 20 QR scans per shift by week 3, move demos to the top 3 stores; creator click rate under 1%, shift spend to Meta [A4].
slides.notes: Test vs. control is what a CPG buyer wants: proof the lift came from the campaign.

slides.title: Why It Matters
bullets: Thesis: All Y'Alls does not need more doors - it needs shoppers who try it once to come back. The Smarter Switch turns H-E-B shelf space into repeat buyers [O1].
Projected: 1,500 purchases and $16.5K gross profit on $10K (65% ROI), plus a test-vs-control result All Y'Alls can take to every retailer [A1][O1].
Mission: a Texas jerky that does not compromise - plant protein with real chew, backed by a surgeon and a sanctuary, kept on Texas shelves because Texans tried it [S2][S5].
Next: if test stores beat control by 25%, roll The Smarter Switch to more H-E-B stores and repair the Amazon rating gap [O1].
